prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D Assassin survivor animation for Grave Accord. Image 1 is the approved complete idle strip for this exact facing; it locks identity, camera and equipment grip. Image 2 is the original shipped single-facing seed. Both references show the required direction; do not invent an opposite-facing view. Preserve the same slim young adult man with tousled black hair, visible eyes, lower face covered by a high rust-red scarf, a single long torn rust-red cape, charcoal split tunic/trousers, layered dark bronze shoulder/forearm/knee armor, brown utility belt pouches, gloves and boots. ONE slender long brass-and-black carbine stays attached to the physical RIGHT hand at the rear trigger grip and LEFT hand under the fore-end. Keep both hands and the rigid weapon connected. Preserve cape/strap asymmetry and original layered shoulder shapes. No exposed mouth, hood, extra pistol, knife, second rifle or weapon swap. Use restrained dry black ink and matte opaque gouache, broad quiet color planes and selective practical contours. Avoid glossy gradients, excessive tiny scratches, decorative filigree or noise. Maintain two arms, two legs and one intact body/weapon in every pose.
Every pose faces NORTH, away from the viewer. We see back of hair/coat/cape, never the face. Retain the exact original back-facing equipment placement. The gun is partly hidden naturally in front of the body, with its visible portion matching the seed. Preserve physical RIGHT trigger and LEFT support grip; do not mirror straps or belt.
Draw EXACTLY 4 full-body poses as one coherent attack sheet, arranged in one horizontal row of 4 complete poses on a wide transparent canvas. No additional figure. Action: One restrained stationary primary shot cycle: 1 upright ready stance matching the reference, 2 raise and brace the SAME gun slightly with both original grips, 3 a small controlled recoil into the shoulders, 4 settle back toward pose 1. Keep boots planted, torso orientation fixed and gun barrel rigid. No broad swing, torso spin or grip exchange. Do not draw muzzle flash, projectile, casing, smoke, spark or any effect; the game renders effects separately.
Every pose is one complete independent drawn body at ONE common character scale calibrated from upright pose 1. Crouched and resting poses retain their naturally lower height. Use roomy clear gutters between all cells and generous padding around the ENTIRE body/weapon/cape, with a consistent ground baseline in each row. Genuine RGBA transparency: alpha zero outside each figure and between limbs/props. No floor, shadow, backdrop, haze, vignette, glow, particles, checker pattern, text, labels, frame numbers or grid lines. Keep a coherent animation rather than unrelated character illustrations.
CRITICAL SHEET LAYOUT CORRECTION: adjacent figures must be completely disconnected. Use a visibly roomy sheet with equal cells and make ALL poses uniformly smaller inside those cells. Each upright figure occupies only about 55 percent of its CELL HEIGHT; the entire body, cape and full-length rifle must stay inside the middle 70 percent of that CELL WIDTH. Keep at least one whole head-width of perfectly transparent space between ANY neighboring silhouettes, including extended rifle barrels and trailing cape tips. All rifle/cape/limb pixels belong to one complete figure and never touch or overlap the next figure. Preserve original body and full rifle proportions while scaling every figure down uniformly. Keep the same approved facing, hands, mask and camera; do not introduce a different view. The extra padding is intentional production space.
